access.md.note: Every token, deploy key, deploy token, access request, invite, and job-token-scoped tool, plus the CRUD half of project/group member management. The README row says 'various' — the team hand-curated these tools and this allowlist mirrors that.

admin.md.note: Owns the audit-event surface (Premium group gitlab_audit_event has no dedicated meta-tool doc). The README Domains table doesn't list this group; audit events live here by team convention (admin is the natural home for instance-level endpoints).

analytics-compliance.md.note: README lists gitlab_group (enterprise routes), gitlab_compliance_policy, gitlab_project_alias. DORA metrics is documented here too, but its group name is gitlab_dora_metrics, not gitlab_group.

boards.md.note: Owns the board/label/milestone surfaces even though they live inside gitlab_project/gitlab_group groups. Naming prefixes are how the team distinguishes project-management surfaces from core project CRUD.

branches.md.note: Owns all gitlab_branch_* and gitlab_protected_branch_* tools (one group, gitlab_branch).

capabilities.md.note: Claims gitlab_server so capabilities.md owns gitlab_server_status and its share of the MCP maintenance surface. Without this, the first-claimer rule (admin.md claims gitlab_server earlier) would route gitlab_server_status to admin.md.

ci-cd.md.note: The README row lists gitlab_pipeline, gitlab_job, 'etc.' but omits the adjacent groups that build the rest of the CI/CD surface (CI variables, CI lint, CI catalog).

epics.md.note: Owns the epic core surface (epics, epic notes, epic issues, epic discussions, group epic boards). These tools live in the gitlab_group catalog group; the README's 'gitlab_epic' entry is a routing label rather than a real group, so the prefix allowlist is the canonical ownership signal.

identity-security.md.note: README lists gitlab_group_scim, gitlab_member_role, 'etc.' The 'etc.' captures the enterprise routes inside gitlab_group / gitlab_project.

integrations.md.note: Owns the integration/badge/topic/import surface that lives inside gitlab_project and gitlab_group. Epic-discussion tools are intentionally absent — they live in epics.md via the wider 'gitlab_epic_' prefix, which wins under longest-match-wins for the bare tool names too.

merge-requests.md.note: Owns the merge-train and external-status-check surfaces (Premium/Ultimate groups) whose owning catalog group has no dedicated meta-tool doc. The README Domains table doesn't list these groups; they live here by team convention.

mirrors.md.note: Owns a small set of project mirror tools that live inside gitlab_project (per buildProjectActionSpecs). The README's 'gitlab_project (enterprise routes)' annotation is the source.

notifications.md.note: The README row says 'various'. The canonical group it touches is gitlab_notification (global/group/project notification settings); the events surface is owned via the prefix list below.

packages.md.note: Owns the dependency-list surface (Ultimate group 'dependencies' has no dedicated meta-tool doc). The README Domains table doesn't list this group; dependencies live here by team convention (packages is the natural home for inventory / export workflows).

security.md.note: Owns feature flags, secure files, error tracking, alert metric images, impersonation tokens, and the admin-side user-token creation tool (gitlab_create_personal_access_token). The PAT listing tools live in access.md via the 'personal_access_token_' prefix; admin-user PAT creation lives here.

tags.md.note: Owns all gitlab_tag_* and gitlab_protected_tag_* tools. Note: gitlab_tag_protect is a mutating tool; the auditor's destructive detection handles the Write annotation.
